usage: Refers to a leaf that is still new, soft, and not fully grown yet. It is often used in gardening, botany, and nature descriptions.
Commonly used with plants, tea, vegetables, and tree growth when talking about fresh new foliage rather than mature leaves.
In Cantonese, it sounds natural in written and spoken descriptive language, especially when you want to be precise about plant stages.
Good learner tip: this word focuses on age/stage of the leaf, so it is different from a general word for leaf. Use it when the leaf is young, tender, or newly sprouted.
